builds.howItPlays: You take one battlefield and dig in with sturdy units like Sona, Harmonious and Blue Sentinel, which gets +2 Might while defending and makes each point you score by holding its battlefield count twice, while Ahri gives every enemy that attacks there -1 Might. You answer their plays on their turn with spells, then set Temporal Breach face down and later use it to play your Thousand-Tailed Watcher again for free, so its -3 Might to every enemy unit hits a second time.
builds.whyYou: You'd rather let your opponent come to you and make them pay for it. You like picking one spot on the board, making it hard to take, and keeping spells ready for their turn instead of racing them. Games run long and you don't mind, because every turn you hold that battlefield is another point, and a well-timed replay of your big unit usually settles it. If a stubborn defense that slowly pulls ahead sounds more fun than an early knockout, this Ahri suits you.
